facts.text: I have pain in my belly.

facts.item: how long the tiredness and belly pain have been going on
facts.text: The tiredness and the belly pain have been going on for the past 4 weeks.
I've been having excessive night sweats.
I've noticeably lost weight, about 5.4 kg (12 lb).
I noticed a swelling in my neck.
It came up over the last 4 days.

facts.item: feeling of fullness in the belly
facts.text: My belly feels unusually full, and I have trouble wearing my usual clothes because of it.
I don't have any significant medical problems, and I haven't had any major illnesses before.
I haven't had any major surgeries.
I smoke 1 pack a day, and I have for the past 30 years.
I work for a construction company.

findings.name: neck examination
findings.result: Nontender, enlarged, fixed supraclavicular lymph node.

findings.name: abdominal examination
findings.result: Inspection: slight abdominal distension; auscultation: normal bowel sounds; percussion: dullness over the left lower quadrant; palpation: splenomegaly, without rebound tenderness.

findings.name: complete blood count
findings.result: WBC elevated; hemoglobin slightly decreased; platelets normal.

findings.name: CT of the chest and abdomen
findings.result: Massively enlarged axillary, mediastinal and cervical lymph nodes.

findings.name: cervical lymph node biopsy
findings.result: Lymphocytes with a high proliferative index that stain positive for CD20.

f004: The History reads 'fatigue, worsening abdominal pain for the past 4 weeks, excessive night sweats, ...': the 4 weeks follows the abdominal pain and most naturally covers fatigue and pain together. Night sweats and weight loss are given no time frame and are left without one.

x005.source_text: Nontender, enlarged, and fixed supraclavicular lymph node observed.

x006.source_text: Slight abdominal distension. + Normal bowel sounds. + Dullness noted over the left lower quadrant. + Splenomegaly detected, without rebound tenderness.

x009.source_text: Massively enlarged axillary, mediastinal, and cervical lymph nodes.

x010.source_text: Lymphocytes with a high proliferative index that stain positive for CD20.

x006: Percussion dullness is placed over the left lower quadrant while palpation finds splenomegaly (the spleen lies in the left upper quadrant); kept as written.

source_issues: Abdominal percussion reports dullness over the left lower quadrant alongside splenomegaly; plausible for a massively enlarged spleen but unusual wording.
Temperature 36.8°C is given as 98°F (98.2°F by conversion); rounding only.
notes: The chief complaint names two complaints (fatigue, abdominal pain), so both facts open the case.
The 4-week duration applies to two symptoms, so it is a standalone fact (f004) rather than a child.
The belly fullness with difficulty wearing usual clothing (ROS) is one statement (f009); it is kept separate from abdominal pain.
'No previous major illnesses or surgeries' gives two denials: major illnesses joins the past-medical-history denial (f013), surgeries is f014.
check_coverage warns that x007's alias 'white blood cell count' contains the gold word 'cell'. Kept: it is the standard clinical name of the test and reveals nothing about B-cell lymphoma.

extras.objective_for_doctor: Evaluate and diagnose the patient presenting with fatigue, abdominal pain, night sweats, weight loss, and enlarged supraclavicular lymph node.
